privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro:
At Cashvio, your trust is the foundation of everything we build. This Privacy Policy explains what information we collect, why we collect it, how we use and protect it, and the rights and choices you have over it.

It applies to the Cashvio website, the merchant dashboard, the point-of-sale applications, online storefronts we host for merchants, and all related services (together, the "Services"). By using the Services, you acknowledge that you have read and understood this policy.

scope.title: Who We Are and Scope of This Policy
scope.content:
The Services are operated by Cashvio Technologies ("Cashvio", "we", "us", or "our"), headquartered in Cairo, Egypt.

We act in two distinct roles. For the personal information of merchants, their staff, and visitors to our own websites, we are the data controller — we decide how and why that information is processed. For the information that merchants store about their own customers (such as customer profiles and purchase history), we act as a data processor — we process it only on the merchant's behalf and instructions, as described in the section "Your Customers' Data" below.

collection.title: Information We Collect
collection.content: We collect information in three ways: information you provide to us directly, information generated automatically when you use the Services, and information we receive from third parties (such as payment providers confirming a transaction). This includes:
items: Account information — your name, email address, phone number, password (stored only in hashed form), preferred language, and profile settings.
Business information — your business name, store names and addresses, business type, tax and registration details, logo and branding assets.
Transaction and operations data — orders, invoices, receipts, refunds, payment methods used, product catalogs, inventory movements, shift records, and reports generated from them.
Billing information — the subscription plan you choose and billing history. Card payments are processed by licensed payment providers; we never store full card numbers on our servers.
Customer records you create — information about your own customers that you enter into the platform, such as their names, contact details, purchase history, balances, and store credit.
Device and usage data — IP address, browser and device type, operating system, pages visited, features used, referral URLs, timestamps, and crash or error diagnostics.
Cookies and similar technologies — as described in the "Cookies and Analytics" section below.
Communications — messages, support requests, feedback, and recordings of support conversations where permitted by law.

usage.title: How We Use Your Information
usage.content: We use the information we collect only for purposes that are compatible with running, protecting, and improving the Services:
items: Provide and operate the Services — creating your account, running your point of sale and storefront, processing orders, and syncing your data across devices.
Secure the platform — authenticating logins, enforcing permissions, detecting and preventing fraud, abuse, and unauthorized access.
Support you — responding to your questions, troubleshooting problems, and notifying you about incidents that affect your account.
Improve and develop — analyzing aggregated usage patterns to fix issues, improve performance, and build new features.
Communicate — sending service announcements, security alerts, billing notices, and (with your consent or where permitted) product news and offers you can opt out of at any time.
Comply with the law — meeting our accounting, tax, and other legal obligations, and responding to lawful requests from authorities.
usage.footer: We do not use your business data — such as your sales figures, margins, or customer lists — to compete with you, and we never sell it to third parties.

legalBases.title: Legal Bases for Processing
legalBases.content: Where data protection law requires a legal basis for processing (such as the EU GDPR or similar laws), we rely on: performance of our contract with you (to deliver the Services you signed up for); our legitimate interests (to secure, improve, and market the Services in ways that do not override your rights); your consent (for optional marketing and non-essential cookies, which you can withdraw at any time); and compliance with legal obligations (such as retaining tax records).

customerData.title: Your Customers' Data
customerData.content:
When you record information about your own customers in Cashvio — for example a customer profile, order history, or store credit balance — you are the data controller of that information and we process it strictly on your behalf.

We process such data only to provide the Services to you, never for our own marketing, and we do not contact your customers except as needed to deliver features you actively use (such as sending a digital receipt at your request). You are responsible for collecting your customers' data lawfully, informing them about how it is used, and honoring their privacy requests. If a customer contacts us directly about data you control, we will refer them to you and provide reasonable assistance.

sharing.title: How We Share Information
sharing.content: We do not sell, rent, or trade your personal information. We share it only in these limited circumstances:
items: Service providers — companies that help us run the platform, such as cloud hosting, payment processing, email and SMS delivery, push notifications, and analytics. They may only use the data to provide their service to us and are bound by contractual confidentiality and data-protection obligations.
Payment providers — when you or your customers make a payment, the transaction details are shared with the licensed payment provider handling it.
Legal requirements — when required by applicable law, regulation, legal process, or an enforceable governmental request, and only to the extent required.
Protecting rights and safety — to enforce our terms, investigate fraud or security issues, or protect the rights, property, or safety of Cashvio, our merchants, or the public.

Business transfers — if Cashvio is involved in a merger, acquisition, or sale of assets, your information may be transferred as part of that transaction. We will notify you before your data becomes subject to a different privacy policy.
Aggregated or anonymized data — we may share statistics that cannot reasonably be used to identify you or your customers.

cookies.title: Cookies and Analytics
cookies.content:
We use cookies and similar technologies to keep you signed in, remember your preferences (such as language and theme), protect against fraud, and understand how the Services are used so we can improve them.

Essential cookies are required for the Services to function and cannot be switched off. Analytics cookies help us measure feature usage and performance in aggregate. You can control non-essential cookies through your browser settings; blocking essential cookies may prevent parts of the Services from working correctly.

transfers.title: International Data Transfers
transfers.content: We may store and process your information on servers located outside the country where you live, including through cloud infrastructure providers operating in multiple regions. Whenever we transfer personal information across borders, we take steps to ensure it receives an adequate and consistent level of protection, including contractual safeguards with our service providers, and we comply with applicable data-transfer requirements.

retention.title: Data Retention
retention.content:
We keep your information for as long as your account is active and as needed to provide the Services. Transaction and billing records are retained for the period required by applicable tax, accounting, and commercial laws even after account closure.

When retention is no longer necessary, we delete or irreversibly anonymize the data. Residual copies may persist in encrypted backups for a limited period until those backups expire on their regular cycle.

security.title: How We Protect Your Data
security.content: We apply layered technical and organizational safeguards designed to protect your information against unauthorized access, alteration, disclosure, or destruction:
items: Encryption in transit (TLS) for all connections and encryption at rest for stored data.
Passwords stored using strong one-way hashing — we can never read your password.
Strict tenant isolation, so one business's data is never visible to another.
Role-based access controls and the principle of least privilege for both our systems and your staff accounts.
Continuous monitoring, logging, and automated alerting for suspicious activity.
Regular backups and a tested incident-response process.
security.footer: No system can be guaranteed 100% secure, but if we become aware of a breach affecting your personal information, we will notify you and the relevant authorities without undue delay, as required by law.

rights.title: Your Rights and Choices
rights.content: Depending on where you live, you may have some or all of the following rights regarding your personal information:
items: Access — request a copy of the personal information we hold about you.
Correction — ask us to fix inaccurate or incomplete information.
Deletion — ask us to delete your personal information, subject to legal retention requirements.
Portability — receive your data in a structured, commonly used, machine-readable format.
Objection and restriction — object to or ask us to limit certain processing.
Withdraw consent — where processing is based on consent, withdraw it at any time without affecting prior processing.
Complain — lodge a complaint with your local data-protection authority.
rights.footer: To exercise any of these rights, contact us using the details below. We may need to verify your identity before acting on a request, and we will respond within the timeframe required by applicable law (and in any case within 30 days wherever feasible).

marketing.title: Marketing Communications
marketing.content: We may send you news about features, tips, and offers related to Cashvio. You can opt out at any time using the unsubscribe link in any marketing email or through your notification settings. Opting out does not affect essential service communications, such as security alerts, billing notices, and legal or policy updates.

children.title: Children's Privacy
children.content: The Services are business tools and are not directed at children. We do not knowingly collect personal information from anyone under 16 years of age. If you believe a child has provided us with personal information, please contact us and we will delete it promptly.

changes.title: Changes to This Policy
changes.content: We may update this Privacy Policy from time to time to reflect changes in the Services, technology, or the law. If we make material changes, we will notify you by email or through a prominent notice in the Services before the changes take effect, and we will update the "Last updated" date above. We encourage you to review this page periodically.

contact.title: Contact Us
contact.content: If you have any questions, concerns, or requests regarding this Privacy Policy or how we handle your data, contact our privacy team at support@cashvio.com or write to Cashvio Technologies, Cairo, Egypt. We aim to respond to every privacy inquiry promptly.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.subtitle: Everything you need to know about creating and managing coupons in Cashvio.

q1.question: What types of discounts can I create?
q1.answer: Cashvio supports two discount types: percentage off (0-100%) and fixed amount off in your store's currency. Both apply to the whole order subtotal.

q2.question: Can I use the same coupon code across multiple stores?
q2.answer: Each coupon belongs to one store. If you want the same promotion across multiple locations, create a coupon with the same code in each store. This gives you independent control over usage limits and status per location.

q3.question: How do I prevent customers from abusing a coupon code?
q3.answer: Set a per-customer usage limit (e.g., 1 for one-time use). Combined with a total usage cap, you control exactly how many times a code can be redeemed overall and per individual buyer.

q4.question: Can customers use multiple coupons on a single order?
q4.answer: Currently, one coupon can be applied per order. This keeps discount stacking predictable and protects your margins.

q5.question: Do coupons work on both the POS and the online store?
q5.answer: Yes. Customers can enter coupon codes during online storefront checkout, and your cashiers can apply codes during POS order creation. The same validation rules apply in both channels.

q6.question: Can I schedule a coupon to start on a future date?
q6.answer: Yes. Set a Valid From date in the future when creating the coupon. Keep the coupon status inactive until launch day, then toggle it to active when your campaign starts.

q7.question: What happens when a coupon reaches its usage limit?
q7.answer: The coupon automatically becomes unusable — customers who try to apply it will see an error. The coupon stays visible in your list so you can view its history or increase the limit.

q8.question: Can I edit a coupon after creation?
q8.answer: Yes, you can edit the code, discount type and value, minimum cart value, usage limits, validity dates, and active status. The only field you cannot change is the store assignment.

q9.question: What happens to past orders if I delete a coupon?
q9.answer: Past orders retain their discount information even after coupon deletion. The coupon data is preserved in order history, so your financial records remain accurate.

q10.question: Is there a free plan that includes coupon management?
q10.answer: Yes. Coupon management is available on all Cashvio plans, including the free forever plan. Create and manage discount codes without upgrading.

q1.answer: No. Reports build themselves from your sales, orders, customers, and returns. The one thing worth doing: set cost prices on your product variants so profit reports are accurate.

q2.question: How is profit calculated?
q2.answer: Profit uses the cost price you set on each product variant: selling price minus cost. Keep cost prices up to date — especially when supplier prices change — and your margins stay honest.

q3.question: Can I compare this month to last month?
q3.answer: Yes, automatically. Every metric shows its change versus the previous period — pick month view and each number compares against the month before.

q4.question: Can I see numbers per branch?
q4.answer: Yes. The Sales by Store chart splits revenue per branch, and clicking a branch opens its orders. Store comparisons run through the reports.

q5.question: Can I see sales per employee?
q5.answer: Yes. The Staff tab shows revenue per team member, orders processed per person, and how each person's performance trends over time.

q6.question: What exactly does the Insights tab tell me?
q6.answer: It converts your numbers into plain-language guidance: health scores per area, critical issues, warnings, opportunities, and recent wins — each with recommended actions, expected impact, and priority.

q7.question: Can I export the data?
q7.answer: Yes. The Overview tab exports its sales data to CSV so you can work with it in any spreadsheet or hand it to your accountant.

q8.question: Do returns and refunds show up in the numbers?
q8.answer: Yes. Refunded amounts are reflected in the relevant metrics, and the Returns tab breaks down return rate, reasons, most-returned products, and the total value of returns.

problem.title: Restocking by Phone Call Leaves No Trace
problem.subtitle: A voice note to the supplier, a price agreed on the phone, a delivery checked by memory — until quantities do not match and nobody can prove anything.

noRecord.title: Orders With No Record
noRecord.description: You ordered twenty, the supplier remembers fifteen, the invoice says eighteen. Without a written purchase order, every disagreement is your word against theirs.

costsUntracked.title: Costs Nobody Tracks
costsUntracked.description: Supplier prices creep up delivery by delivery. If cost per item is not recorded at order time, your margins shrink quietly and your profit reports lie.

uncheckedDeliveries.title: Deliveries Checked by Memory
uncheckedDeliveries.description: Boxes arrive, someone shelves them, and the count in your head becomes the count in your stock. Missing items are discovered weeks later — too late to claim.

partialLost.title: Partial Deliveries Fall Through

features.title: The Full Restocking Cycle, Recorded

howItWorks.title: From Low Stock to Full Shelves
howItWorks.subtitle: Three steps, and every one of them leaves a record.

step1.title: Create the Purchase Order
step1.description: Low stock alerts tell you what needs reordering. Create a PO: pick the store and supplier, add products with quantities and agreed costs, set the expected delivery date.

step2.title: Approve It
step2.description: Review the draft and approve it by typing APPROVE. The order is now official — waiting for delivery, visible to your team, and impossible to lose.

step3.title: Receive the Stock
step3.description: When boxes arrive, enter the received quantity per item — all of it or just what came. Stock goes up instantly, and the PO closes itself when everything is in.

effects.title: What Each Step Does to Your Inventory

created.effect: Nothing changes — it is a record of intent, not stock

received.effect: Inventory increases by the received quantities, each receipt logged as an adjustment

cancelled.effect: Nothing changes — the order is voided with no stock movement

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.subtitle: Common questions about purchase orders and suppliers in Cashvio.

q1.question: Can I receive a delivery in parts?
q1.answer: Yes. Enter the quantity that actually arrived per item — the PO becomes Partially Received and keeps tracking the remaining quantities until everything is in, then completes itself.

q2.question: Does creating a purchase order change my stock?
q2.answer: No. Creating and approving a PO changes nothing in inventory — it is a record of what you ordered. Stock only increases when you receive it, by the quantities you actually received.

q3.question: What do I need to add a supplier?
q3.answer: Just the supplier's name. Email, phone, and address are optional. You can also add a supplier on the fly from the supplier picker while creating a purchase order.

q4.question: Can I see everything I ordered from one supplier?
q4.answer: Yes. The supplier's page shows their full purchase order history — with the same view, approve, cancel, and receive actions as the main PO list — plus a button to start a new PO with them pre-selected.

q5.question: How do I avoid approving an order by mistake?
q5.answer: Approval requires typing APPROVE in a confirmation dialog, and cancelling requires typing CANCEL. Accidental clicks cannot approve or kill an order.

q6.question: Can I add delivery fees to a purchase order?
q6.answer: Yes. Delivery fees and notes are set in the second step of PO creation, alongside the expected delivery date.

q7.question: How do purchase orders help my profit reports?
q7.answer: POs record the unit cost you agreed with the supplier. Combined with the cost prices on your product variants, the Profit report can show real margins and cost breakdowns by supplier.

q8.question: Can I limit who is allowed to approve purchase orders?
q8.answer: Yes. Purchase order permissions are fine-grained — view, create, edit, approve, receive, and cancel are separate permissions you assign per role.

hero.title: Returns & Refunds
hero.subtitle: A clear process for the least fun part of retail: item-level returns with recorded reasons, control over what goes back on the shelf, an approval step, and four refund methods — including store credit that keeps the money in your business.

problem.title: Messy Returns Cost More Than the Refund
problem.subtitle: Every shop gets returns. The damage is not the return itself — it is the missing record, the wrong stock count, and the cash that left the drawer with no trace.

noProcess.title: Every Return Is a Negotiation
noProcess.description: No process means whoever is at the counter decides. One employee refunds everything, another refuses everything — and customers learn to argue.

stockWrong.title: Returned Items Vanish
stockWrong.description: The item came back, but did it go back into stock? Was it damaged? Without restock tracking, returns quietly corrupt your inventory counts.

cashLeaks.title: Refunds With No Record
cashLeaks.description: Cash handed back from the drawer with no paper trail. At the end of the month, the numbers do not add up and nobody remembers why.

noReasons.title: No Idea Why Things Come Back
noReasons.description: Wrong size? Damaged in delivery? Quality problems? If reasons are not recorded, you keep buying and selling the same mistakes.

returnTypes.title: Three Return Types, Because Reality Has Three
returnTypes.subtitle: Not every return needs a refund, and not every refund involves goods coming back. Pick the type that matches the situation.

returnRefund.title: Return & Refund
returnRefund.description: The classic case: the customer brings the items back and gets their money. Items are checked back in, and the refund is created with the return.

returnOnly.title: Return Only
returnOnly.description: Goods come back with no money out — an exchange, a warranty case, or store policy. Inventory is corrected without touching the cash.

refundOnly.title: Refund Only
refundOnly.description: Money goes back with no goods returned — a compensation, a goodwill gesture, or an item the customer keeps. The refund is recorded against the order.

features.title: Every Detail of the Return, Handled
features.subtitle: Item by item, reason by reason — the return flow asks the right questions so your stock and your money stay correct.

itemLevel.name: Item-Level Returns
itemLevel.description: Pick exactly which items and quantities come back. The system knows what was already returned and only offers what is still returnable.
itemLevel.subs: Per-Item Quantities • Returnable Check • Partial Returns

restockControl.name: Restock Control
restockControl.description: Decide per item whether it goes back into sellable stock. Damaged, expired, or contaminated items are marked with a non-restock reason instead — never resold by accident.
restockControl.subs: Restock Toggle • Non-Restock Reasons • Condition Notes

restockingFee.name: Restocking Fees
restockingFee.description: Charge a restocking fee on returned items when your policy calls for it — recorded on the return, deducted from the refund.

reasons.name: Recorded Return Reasons
reasons.description: Every return carries a reason — changed mind, wrong item, defective, damaged, size issue, and more. Reasons feed the Returns report so patterns become visible.

approval.name: Approval Flow
approval.description: Returns are created as pending, then approved, rejected, or cancelled — rejections and cancellations require a written reason. Stock only moves on approval.
approval.subs: Pending → Approved • Reject With Reason • Audit Trail

refundMethods.name: Four Refund Methods
refundMethods.description: Cash from the drawer, online for digital payments, receipt-documented transfers, or store credit added to the customer's balance.

pendingProcess.name: Refunds Processed Deliberately
pendingProcess.description: Creating a refund does not move money by itself. A pending refund is processed explicitly — or cancelled with a reason — so the books match the drawer.
pendingProcess.subs: Pending → Completed • Explicit Processing • Cancel With Reason

partialRefunds.name: Full or Partial Refunds
partialRefunds.description: Refund a specific payment or any custom amount up to what is still refundable on the order. The order's payment history shows every refund.
partialRefunds.subs: Specific Payment • Custom Amount • Refund History

howItWorks.title: A Return in Three Clean Steps
howItWorks.subtitle: From the moment the customer walks back in to the moment the money and stock are settled.

step1.title: Create the Return From the Order
step1.description: Open the original order and click Create Return. Choose the type, select the items and quantities, decide restocking per item, and record the reason.

step2.title: Approve It
step2.description: A pending return is reviewed and approved — or rejected with a written reason. On approval, restockable items go back into inventory automatically.

step3.title: Refund the Money
step3.description: Create the refund — full or partial — pick the method, and process it. Store credit refunds land on the customer's balance the moment they are processed.

refundMethods.title: Refund Methods for How Money Actually Moves
refundMethods.subtitle: Each method is recorded against the order, so the payment history always tells the full story.

cash.when: The customer paid cash and wants cash back — straight from the drawer, recorded

online.when: Refunding a digital payment — available when the original payment was online

receipt.when: A bank or wallet transfer documented with proof of the refund

storeCredit.when: The refund becomes balance on the customer's account — money stays in your business

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.subtitle: Common questions about returns and refunds in Cashvio.

q1.question: Can I refund without taking items back?
q1.answer: Yes — that is the Refund Only type. Money is returned against the order with no return record and no inventory movement. Useful for compensations and goodwill gestures.

q2.question: Can I take items back without refunding?
q2.answer: Yes — Return Only. The items are returned and restocked (or marked non-restockable) with no money out. Useful for exchanges and warranty flows.

q3.question: When does returned stock go back into inventory?
q3.answer: When the return is approved. Items you marked as restockable are added back to the store's stock; items with a non-restock reason (damaged, expired, etc.) are not.

q4.question: Does approving a return automatically refund the money?
q4.answer: No — returns and refunds are separate deliberate steps. Approving a return settles the goods; you then create and process a refund to settle the money. Nothing moves by accident.

q5.question: How does a store credit refund work?
q5.answer: Choose Store Credit as the refund method (the order must have a customer attached). When the refund is processed, the amount is added to the customer's balance — which they can spend on any future order.

q6.question: Can I refund part of an order?
q6.answer: Yes. Refund a specific payment or enter a custom amount up to what is still refundable on the order. Every refund appears in the order's refund history.

q7.question: Can I charge a restocking fee?
q7.answer: Yes. When restocking a returned item you can add a restocking fee — it is recorded on the return and reflected in the refund amount.

q8.question: Do returns show up in my reports?
q8.answer: Yes. The Returns report shows your return rate, the reasons breakdown, the most-returned products, and the total value of returns — so recurring problems surface instead of repeating.

hero.subtitle: Each branch keeps its own stock, prices, payment methods, and receipts — and you see all of them from one dashboard. Transfer stock between stores, limit staff to their branch, and compare branches side by side.

problem.title: The Second Branch Doubles the Chaos
problem.subtitle: One shop fits in your head. Two do not. The moment you open a second branch, every question — stock, prices, staff, numbers — has two answers that do not talk to each other.

islands.title: Every Branch Is an Island
islands.description: Separate spreadsheets, separate registers, separate WhatsApp groups. Getting one picture of the business means calling every branch and doing the math yourself.

stockBlindness.title: Nobody Knows What the Other Branch Has
stockBlindness.description: A customer wants a size that is out here — is it available downtown? Without shared visibility, the answer is a phone call, a wait, and often a lost sale.

priceDrift.title: Prices Drift Apart
priceDrift.description: A price update reaches one branch and not the other. Customers notice before you do — and it never feels good to explain.

noComparison.title: No Way to Compare Branches
noComparison.description: Which branch actually earns? Which one has a returns problem? Gut answers only, unless the numbers live in one system.

features.title: Independent Branches, One Command Center

step3.description: Staff sell in their own branch; you watch all branches from one dashboard — stock, orders, and revenue per store, compared automatically.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.subtitle: Common questions about running multiple stores in Cashvio.

q1.question: How many stores can I create?
q1.answer: It depends on your plan — each plan includes a number of stores. Your first store is created automatically when you sign up, and you can add more from Settings as your plan allows.

q2.question: Can I move stock from one branch to another?
q2.answer: Yes. Stock transfers move quantities between stores with a full record — what moved, from where, to where, and when. No spreadsheet reconciliation.

q3.question: Can branches have different prices?
q3.answer: Yes. Prices are shared by default, and you can set store-specific prices per product variant where branches need to differ.

q4.question: Can each store use a different currency?
q4.answer: Yes. Currency is set per store — useful when branches operate in different markets.

q5.question: Can I restrict an employee to a single branch?
q5.answer: Yes. When assigning a role to a user, choose store-specific and pick the branch. They see and do only what their role allows, only in that store.

q6.question: Can I see one branch's numbers separately?
q6.answer: Yes. Reports break down by store — revenue share per branch, plus filters across orders and inventory. Click a branch in the Sales by Store chart to open its orders.

q7.question: What happens when I deactivate a store?
q7.answer: The branch stops accepting new activity but loses nothing — its history, stock records, and settings stay intact. You can reactivate it any time.

q8.question: Do my products need to be recreated per store?
q8.answer: No. The product catalogue is shared across your whole business. Each store only maintains its own stock levels and, if you choose, its own prices.

hero.subtitle: Stop sharing the owner's password. Give each team member their own account with exactly the permissions their job needs — a cashier sells, an accountant sees money, a warehouse worker touches stock — and every action is recorded under their name.

problem.title: One Shared Password Is a Business Risk
problem.subtitle: When everyone logs in as the owner, everyone is the owner. No limits, no accountability, and no way to take access back when someone leaves.

sharedLogin.title: Everyone Uses the Owner's Account
sharedLogin.description: The whole team on one login means every employee can see profits, change prices, delete products, and cancel orders — whether they should or not.

noAccountability.title: Nobody Owns Any Action
noAccountability.description: An order was cancelled and a discount appeared. Who did it? With one shared account, the honest answer is: no idea.

allOrNothing.title: Access Is All or Nothing
allOrNothing.description: You want the new hire to ring up sales — not to see revenue reports or edit the catalogue. Without roles, you cannot give one without the other.

exStaffRisk.title: Ex-Employees Keep the Keys
exStaffRisk.description: Someone leaves, and the password they know still works. Changing it means telling everyone the new one — and the cycle repeats.

customRoles.description: Create as many roles as your team needs — a Warehouse Staff role limited to inventory and purchase orders, a Supervisor role that can cancel orders. Name it, tick the permissions, save.

faq.subtitle: Common questions about team members, roles, and permissions in Cashvio.

q1.question: Does the new team member get an invitation email?
q1.answer: No. Cashvio generates a temporary password and shows it once with a copy button — you share it with the team member yourself, in person or through a channel you trust. If it is lost, set a new password from their profile.

q2.question: What do team members log in with?
q2.answer: Their username or email plus their password. Each person has their own credentials — the owner's password stays with the owner.

q3.question: Can I limit an employee to one branch?
q3.answer: Yes. When assigning their role, check store-specific and pick the store. Their permissions then apply only inside that branch.

q4.question: What are the ready-made roles?

q5.question: Can a role see a page but not change anything?
q5.answer: Yes — grant only the View permission for that resource. Granting any action (create, edit, delete) automatically includes View, because nobody can edit what they cannot see.

q6.question: What happens when an employee leaves?
q6.answer: Deactivate their account — their login stops working immediately, and everything they ever created keeps their name for your records. Reactivate any time if they return.

q7.question: Do role restrictions apply to the business owner?
q7.answer: No. The account owner always has full access to everything. Roles restrict invited team members only.

q8.question: Can I see each employee's sales?
q8.answer: Yes. The Staff report shows revenue per team member, orders processed per person, and performance trends — useful for scheduling, targets, and rewards.
